records.text: Marvin Loh, Cayla Seder 28 August 2026 1 Insights Information Classification: General Jackson Hole 2026 : 3 rd times a charm Unsurprisingly Chairman Warsh did not provide forward guidance in his first Jackson Hole speech; however he did provide enough detail on both his goals and view of the current economy to imply his reaction function. In an apparent attempt to reverse the p oor performance at the July FOMC meeting, he laid out principles that the Fed uses in making policy decisions. Our key takeaway is that if the Fed’s goal is to achieve a balance in supply and demand dynamics, it will need active and forward-looking policy. Importantly more restrictive policy would not conflict with the dual mandate as inflation remains persistently elevated and unemployment remains low. While the Fed has many policy levers to achieve its goal, short term rates are the main tool, and unconventional tools should be reserved for crisis periods. Setting the economic stage: Warsh’s view simply restated the July policy statement and minutes. Principally that growth was resilient, employment was stable and inflation remained elevated. Capex is a large driver for these gains, with credit through public, private and bank channels supporting strong capital demand without signals of financial strains. records.text: ntraday momentum strategies tend to work best in high-volatility periods and event/ correction days, especially where dealers are effectively short gamma (e.g., levered ETF-linked names), with the strongest window being 11AM and 3:30PM. As we identified a poorer performance in a lower volatility underlying such as SPX, we could therefore use it as a carry leg given the ongoing gamma supply from overwriting. We looked at two implementations of the carry. The first one is 3:30PM reversal into the close - we could make a directional sell ATM put or call depending on momentum signal to boost carry in the final 30 minutes. The second one is sell a SPX 1DTE ATM straddle daily on the close against the long SOXX intraday momentum. Lastly, for a final improved strategy, we combined the findings of the 2 carry strategies, with 11:00AM- 3:30PM execution windows while keeping 1% signal, and 50% extra notional for days above 1.5x implied volatility breakeven. We are able to achieve a Sharpe ratio of 2.29 with worst drawdown of 8.4% since 2022. Depending on how the CDU/CSU and SPD fare in the regional elections, there could be implications at the federal level ahead of the next scheduled federal election in 2029. Possible scenarios could include leadership changes at the party level or more wide-ranging changes within the government − even though the German constitution places high hurdles for a change in chancellorship. One potential scenario could include a constructive vote of no confidence under Article 67. This would mean that parliament on its own initiative (without new elections) would elect a new chancellor. If that were to happen, it would imply that the Social Democrats and the CDU/CSU would need to agree on a new chancellor. In another scenario, the chancellor could trigger a vote of confidence, which could be followed by new national elections if he were to lose the vote. Looking ahead, we expect large wage hikes to support private consumption, although growth in consumption is likely to remain moderate for the time being, as inflation rises further from autumn and the boost from durable-goods demand, including autos, runs its course. Capex is expected to remain firm, supported by demand for labor-saving investment to address labor shortages and high corporate profits. In terms of overseas demand, the temporary increase in R&D services that lifted exports in Q2 is likely to drop out, while crude oil import volumes recover, reducing the contribution to growth in Q3. From H2 FY26, fiscal policy under the Takaichi administration also appears likely to contribute modestly to growth. High-income homeowners may be staying put, but they do not appear to be renovating at a pace sufficient to offset other drags. And, as noted earlier, growth in improvement spending has been highly procyclical, closely following existing home sales with a lag. Indeed, existing home sales enter JCHS’s LIRA model with a five- quarter lead. The persistent weakness in sales therefore helps explain why improvements spending has remained weak. This low pace of housing turnover has been abetted, in turn, by elevated financing costs. The financing constraint High mortgage rates have weakened improvement spending through two channels. First, they have reduced housing turn- over and the renovation activity that often accompanies a home purchase. Mortgage rates have remained above 6% since the Fed’s hiking cycle and have risen another 55bp over the past six months (Figure 7). In the PLM regime, you can also add on a shorter duration swap (say 1yr with a notional of $30mm) to further buffer moves in rates. You could also have a larger/ shorter initial swap paired with a smaller forward-starting swap. Then as rates move around, gains/losses on the MBS due to rates can be matched with the same from the swaps hedge. One key distinction is that changes in value from something like spread widening will still flow into income. PLM gives banks another tool for managing longer duration securities; while they might want some duration in their portfolios, the post 2022 period has made that more challenging, and PLM allows them to convert some of those fixed assets in AFS to floating both in eco- nomic and accounting terms. Summary This report summarises key macroeconomic metrics and frameworks that we are closely monitoring. We provide a regular update on the evolution of developed market (DM) rates markets in the recent past. Considering the uncertainty surrounding trade and fiscal policy, we begin by comparing budget balances and current account balances across major DM countries. We then analyse the distribution of outstanding bonds by investor type to assess the proportion held by price-insensitive investors, such as domestic central banks. Moving to market pricing, we examine pricing trends of major central banks, followed by recent market movements in key rates products. Finally, we update our cross -country PCA of term premia, as well as the seasonality of selected rates instrum ents. Definitions, methodologies, links to our key views, and recent publications are provided in the appendix. All 5s10s cash term premia have also moved higher, with NGBs the only exception. Source: IMF, Bloomberg, Citi Research Source: IMF, Citi Research Reversal of USD strength relative to European currencies now shifting to relative to Asian currencies Of course there is no guarantee that such an attempt would be successful even if it were actually tried. In particular, if a EURJPY intervention were to be carried out again, as was the case four weeks ago, to correct JPY weakness, Europe would be unlikely to welcome a large-scale sale of euro-denominated assets. In addition, the main cause of the JPY depreciation this year is seen as JPY-selling hedges accompanying the rise in Japanese stock prices. Even if the BoJ accelerates its monetary normalization process, downward pressure on the JPY is unlikely to disappear easily as long as stock market sentiment remains bullish. That being said, the overall strengthening of the USD that started around 2010 began to taper off in about 2022, and last year there was a progressive reversal of the strength of the USD against the EUR and other European currencies (Figure 7).
